package neo4jcorpus

import (
	"context"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/neo4j/neo4j-go-driver/v5/neo4j"
	"github.com/neo4j/neo4j-go-driver/v5/neo4j/dbtype"
)

// node is the shape the driver hands a decoder: a Props map holding the
// Go values neo4j.PropertyValue names, and nothing else. Every value in
// every test below is one a Bolt hydrator can actually build — an
// integer of any width arrives as int64, a float of any width as
// float64, and an array of anything but bytes as []any.
func node(props map[string]any) dbtype.Node {
	return dbtype.Node{Id: 1, ElementId: "4:corpus:1", Labels: []string{"Corpus"}, Props: props}
}

// recordTx is the record shape the driver hands a query method, bound
// through the seam the emission offers for one: Queries.WithTx takes a
// caller-owned transaction, so a method body can be run with no
// connection, no session and no driver behind it.
type recordTx struct{ records []*neo4j.Record }

func (t recordTx) Run(context.Context, string, map[string]any) (neo4j.ResultWithContext, error) {
	return recordResult{records: t.records}, nil
}

type recordResult struct{ records []*neo4j.Record }

func (r recordResult) Collect(context.Context) ([]*neo4j.Record, error) { return r.records, nil }

// queriesOver binds a Queries whose every method reads the given rows,
// one []any of column values per row against the shared key order.
func queriesOver(keys []string, rows ...[]any) *Queries {
	records := make([]*neo4j.Record, 0, len(rows))
	for _, values := range rows {
		records = append(records, &neo4j.Record{Keys: keys, Values: values})
	}
	return new(Queries).WithTx(recordTx{records: records})
}

// A list of no declared element shape is the one list whose elements the
// decoder must not narrow. Its declared element type is `any`, a type
// assertion to `any` is false for a nil interface value, and null is
// exactly what such a list exists to be allowed to hold — so narrowing
// it would fail the whole decode on the value it was declared for.
//
// The wants here are also the values the AGE backend produces for the
// same graph data: its agtypeValue maps agtype's inline null to nil (see
// internal/codegen/age/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt, TestAgtypeValue), so
// a caller who moves between the two backends is handed the same list.
func TestBinCarriesNullElements(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodeBin(node(map[string]any{
		"loose": []any{true, nil, 3.5},
		"bag":   []any{int64(1), nil, "x"},
		"piles": []any{[]any{int64(1), nil}, []any{}},
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeBin(nulls) = error %v", err)
	}
	if want := []any{true, nil, 3.5}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Loose, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(nulls).Loose = %#v, want %#v", got.Loose, want)
	}
	if got.Bag == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeBin(nulls).Bag = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := []any{int64(1), nil, "x"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*got.Bag, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(nulls).Bag = %#v, want %#v", *got.Bag, want)
	}
	if got.Piles == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeBin(nulls).Piles = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := [][]any{{int64(1), nil}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*got.Piles, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(nulls).Piles = %#v, want %#v", *got.Piles, want)
	}
}

// Absence and shape on the same three properties: a nullable list the
// graph does not hold reaches the caller as a nil pointer, an empty one
// as an empty list, and a property holding something that is not a list
// at all is refused rather than carried through.
func TestBinNullabilityAndShape(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodeBin(node(map[string]any{"loose": []any{}}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeBin(absent) = error %v", err)
	}
	if got.Loose == nil || len(got.Loose) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(absent).Loose = %#v, want an empty list", got.Loose)
	}
	if got.Bag != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(absent).Bag = %#v, want nil", got.Bag)
	}
	if got.Piles != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(absent).Piles = %#v, want nil", got.Piles)
	}

	if _, err := decodeBin(node(map[string]any{"loose": []any{}, "bag": "not a list"})); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(bag: string) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if _, err := decodeBin(node(map[string]any{"loose": []any{}, "piles": []any{int64(1)}})); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(piles: [int]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if _, err := decodeBin(node(map[string]any{})); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(no loose) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
}

// Every other list is narrowed element by element, because the element
// widths the schema declared are not on the wire: the driver hands back
// []any whatever the schema said, so int32 arrives as int64 and float32
// as float64. []byte and time.Time are the two element carriers that do
// arrive as themselves.
func TestListyNarrowsEachElement(t *testing.T) {
	stamp := time.Date(2024, 3, 1, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	got, err := decodeListy(node(map[string]any{
		"tags":   []any{"a", "b"},
		"ranks":  []any{int64(1), int64(-2)},
		"matrix": []any{[]any{int64(7), int64(8)}, []any{}},
		"blobs":  []any{[]byte{1, 2}, []byte{}},
		"stamps": []any{stamp},
		"depths": []any{0.5, 1.5},
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy = error %v", err)
	}
	if want := []string{"a", "b"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Tags, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy().Tags = %#v, want %#v", got.Tags, want)
	}
	if want := []int32{1, -2}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Ranks, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy().Ranks = %#v, want %#v", got.Ranks, want)
	}
	if want := [][]int64{{7, 8}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Matrix, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy().Matrix = %#v, want %#v", got.Matrix, want)
	}
	if want := [][]byte{{1, 2}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Blobs, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy().Blobs = %#v, want %#v", got.Blobs, want)
	}
	if want := []time.Time{stamp}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Stamps, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy().Stamps = %#v, want %#v", got.Stamps, want)
	}
	if got.Depths == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy().Depths = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := []float32{0.5, 1.5}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*got.Depths, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy().Depths = %#v, want %#v", *got.Depths, want)
	}
}

// An empty list is an empty list and not the nil one an absent property
// would reach the caller as. The distinction is the caller's to make, so
// the decoder has to preserve it — and it is the AGE backend's pin too,
// which is what keeps a `len(xs) == 0` check meaning the same thing on
// either backend.
func TestListyEmptyIsNotAbsent(t *testing.T) {
	empty, err := decodeListy(node(map[string]any{
		"tags": []any{}, "ranks": []any{}, "matrix": []any{},
		"blobs": []any{}, "stamps": []any{}, "depths": []any{},
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy(empty) = error %v", err)
	}
	for name, got := range map[string]int{
		"Tags":   len(empty.Tags),
		"Ranks":  len(empty.Ranks),
		"Matrix": len(empty.Matrix),
		"Blobs":  len(empty.Blobs),
		"Stamps": len(empty.Stamps),
	} {
		if got != 0 {
			t.Errorf("decodeListy(empty).%s has %d elements, want 0", name, got)
		}
	}
	if empty.Tags == nil || empty.Ranks == nil || empty.Matrix == nil || empty.Blobs == nil || empty.Stamps == nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(empty) reached a caller with a nil list, want empty ones")
	}
	if empty.Depths == nil || *empty.Depths == nil || len(*empty.Depths) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(empty).Depths = %#v, want a pointer to an empty list", empty.Depths)
	}

	absent, err := decodeListy(node(map[string]any{
		"tags": []any{}, "ranks": []any{}, "matrix": []any{}, "blobs": []any{}, "stamps": []any{},
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy(absent depths) = error %v", err)
	}
	if absent.Depths != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(absent depths).Depths = %#v, want nil", absent.Depths)
	}
}

// A mis-typed element is refused, and the failure names the property and
// the position, because a list is decoded whole and the caller otherwise
// has nothing to go on.
func TestListyRefusesAMisTypedElement(t *testing.T) {
	_, err := decodeListy(node(map[string]any{
		"tags": []any{}, "ranks": []any{int64(1), "no"}, "matrix": []any{},
		"blobs": []any{}, "stamps": []any{},
	}))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy(ranks: [int, string]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"ranks"`, "element 1", "expected int64", "got string"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("decodeListy(ranks: [int, string]) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}
}

// A property of no declared shape is read rather than asserted, so every
// value the graph can hold under it reaches the caller as itself — the
// inline null included, which is the one an assertion could not pass.
func TestAnythingReadsWhatTheGraphHolds(t *testing.T) {
	for _, want := range []any{
		nil, int64(1), 1.5, "x", true,
		[]any{int64(1), nil, "x"},
		map[string]any{"k": "v"},
	} {
		got, err := decodeAnything(node(map[string]any{"payload": want}))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("decodeAnything(payload: %#v) = error %v", want, err)
			continue
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Payload, want) {
			t.Errorf("decodeAnything(payload: %#v).Payload = %#v", want, got.Payload)
		}
	}
}

// Under a nullable one the pointer is what separates the two nulls a
// graph can hold: a property the graph does not have at all, and a
// property it holds whose value is null.
func TestAnythingSeparatesAbsentFromNull(t *testing.T) {
	absent, err := decodeAnything(node(map[string]any{"payload": int64(1)}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(no maybe) = error %v", err)
	}
	if absent.Maybe != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(no maybe).Maybe = %#v, want nil", absent.Maybe)
	}

	held, err := decodeAnything(node(map[string]any{"payload": int64(1), "maybe": nil}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(maybe: null) = error %v", err)
	}
	if held.Maybe == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(maybe: null).Maybe = nil, want a pointer to nil")
	}
	if *held.Maybe != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(maybe: null).Maybe points at %#v, want nil", *held.Maybe)
	}
}

// The one arm that does not go through the driver still has to fail the
// way the driver fails, or a caller could tell which decode path a
// property took from the error text alone.
func TestAnythingMissingPropertyReadsLikeTheDrivers(t *testing.T) {
	n := node(map[string]any{})
	decodeErr := func() error {
		_, err := decodeAnything(n)
		return err
	}()
	if decodeErr == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(no payload) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	_, driverErr := neo4j.GetProperty[int64](n, "payload")
	if driverErr == nil {
		t.Fatalf("neo4j.GetProperty(no payload) = no error")
	}
	if want := "decode Anything.Payload: " + driverErr.Error(); decodeErr.Error() != want {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(no payload) = %q, want %q", decodeErr, want)
	}
}

// Scalars narrow from their carriers the same way list elements do, and
// a nullable one the graph does not hold is a nil pointer rather than a
// pointer to the zero value.
func TestScalarNarrows(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodeScalar(node(map[string]any{
		"id": int64(7), "rank": int64(-3), "active": true, "name": "n", "weight": 0.5,
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeScalar = error %v", err)
	}
	if got.Id != 7 || got.Rank != int32(-3) || !got.Active {
		t.Errorf("decodeScalar() = %#v", got)
	}
	if got.Name == nil || *got.Name != "n" {
		t.Errorf("decodeScalar().Name = %#v, want \"n\"", got.Name)
	}
	if got.Weight == nil || *got.Weight != float32(0.5) {
		t.Errorf("decodeScalar().Weight = %#v, want 0.5", got.Weight)
	}

	absent, err := decodeScalar(node(map[string]any{"id": int64(7), "rank": int64(0), "active": false}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeScalar(absent) = error %v", err)
	}
	if absent.Name != nil || absent.Weight != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeScalar(absent) = %#v, want nil nullables", absent)
	}
}

// A query column carrying a list of no declared element shape is the
// same claim as TestBinCarriesNullElements, one emission over: a column
// is decoded through neo4j.GetRecordValue and a property through the
// Props map, so the two paths narrow independently and a null that
// survives one can still fail the other.
func TestBinColumnsCarryNullElements(t *testing.T) {
	q := queriesOver([]string{"loose", "bag", "piles"}, []any{
		[]any{true, nil, 3.5},
		[]any{int64(1), nil, "x"},
		[]any{[]any{int64(1), nil}, []any{}},
	})
	got, err := q.BinColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("BinColumns(nulls) = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("BinColumns(nulls) returned %d rows, want 1", len(got))
	}
	row := got[0]
	if want := []any{true, nil, 3.5}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Loose, want) {
		t.Errorf("BinColumns(nulls)[0].Loose = %#v, want %#v", row.Loose, want)
	}
	if row.Bag == nil {
		t.Fatalf("BinColumns(nulls)[0].Bag = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := []any{int64(1), nil, "x"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*row.Bag, want) {
		t.Errorf("BinColumns(nulls)[0].Bag = %#v, want %#v", *row.Bag, want)
	}
	if row.Piles == nil {
		t.Fatalf("BinColumns(nulls)[0].Piles = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := [][]any{{int64(1), nil}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*row.Piles, want) {
		t.Errorf("BinColumns(nulls)[0].Piles = %#v, want %#v", *row.Piles, want)
	}
}

// The control on the test above: a column whose elements do have a
// declared width still narrows to it, so "carry the element as it
// arrived" is the rule for the one width that has no narrower carrier
// and not a rule the emission applies everywhere. Both directions are
// here — []byte arrives as itself and is kept, float64 arrives wider
// than the declared float32 and is narrowed — because a decoder that
// carried everything bare would pass on the first alone.
//
// The projection carries two non-nullable list columns rather than one
// because the accumulator each of them builds is a local of the row
// assembly's own scope: under a name shared between them the second
// declaration is `no new variables on left side of :=`, and the
// projection that reaches it is the one no fixture had. A nullable list
// column does not reach it, because its accumulator sits inside the
// `if` its null gate opens.
func TestListyColumnsNarrowEachElement(t *testing.T) {
	q := queriesOver([]string{"tags", "blobs", "depths"}, []any{
		[]any{"a", "b"},
		[]any{[]byte{1, 2}, []byte{}},
		[]any{0.5, 1.5},
	})
	got, err := q.ListyColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns returned %d rows, want 1", len(got))
	}
	row := got[0]
	if want := []string{"a", "b"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Tags, want) {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns()[0].Tags = %#v, want %#v", row.Tags, want)
	}
	if want := [][]byte{{1, 2}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Blobs, want) {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns()[0].Blobs = %#v, want %#v", row.Blobs, want)
	}
	if row.Depths == nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns()[0].Depths = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := []float32{0.5, 1.5}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*row.Depths, want) {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns()[0].Depths = %#v, want %#v", *row.Depths, want)
	}

	// A null column and an empty list stay distinguishable here too, and
	// on this path the distinction is the driver's own: GetRecordValue
	// reports a held null through its second result rather than through
	// the value, so a decoder reading only the value cannot tell them
	// apart.
	null, err := queriesOver([]string{"tags", "blobs", "depths"}, []any{[]any{}, []any{}, nil}).ListyColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns(depths: null) = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(null) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns(depths: null) returned %d rows, want 1", len(null))
	}
	if null[0].Tags == nil || len(null[0].Tags) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns(depths: null)[0].Tags = %#v, want an empty list", null[0].Tags)
	}
	if null[0].Blobs == nil || len(null[0].Blobs) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns(depths: null)[0].Blobs = %#v, want an empty list", null[0].Blobs)
	}
	if null[0].Depths != nil {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns(depths: null)[0].Depths = %#v, want nil", null[0].Depths)
	}

	if _, err := queriesOver([]string{"tags", "blobs", "depths"}, []any{
		[]any{}, []any{"no"}, []any{},
	}).ListyColumns(t.Context()); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns(blobs: [string]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
}

// The element loop nests once per declared list depth, and every level
// of it accumulates into a local of its own. Under a name shared between
// the levels the inner declaration shadows the one the level above
// appends to, so that accumulator and appended value become one
// identifier and the emitted package does not compile. A depth of three
// is the first that reaches it, being the first that puts one such
// declaration inside another.
//
// The two sibling depth-two columns are the control: their loops are
// disjoint blocks, so what the deep columns are refused for is the depth
// and not the count. They are non-nullable so that they are also a
// control for the row assembly's own accumulator, whose collision is on
// column position and which a nullable column hides inside the block its
// null gate opens. No such hiding is available a level down, which is
// what the nullable deep column carries: its loops sit inside that block
// and collide within it just the same.
func TestNestColumnsAccumulateAtEveryDepth(t *testing.T) {
	keys := []string{"cube", "lhs", "rhs", "deep"}
	got, err := queriesOver(keys, []any{
		[]any{[]any{[]any{int64(1), int64(2)}, []any{}}, []any{}},
		[]any{[]any{int64(3)}, []any{int64(4), int64(5)}},
		[]any{[]any{"a"}, []any{}},
		[]any{[]any{[]any{"x"}}},
	}).NestColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("NestColumns(nested) = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("NestColumns(nested) returned %d rows, want 1", len(got))
	}
	row := got[0]
	if want := [][][]int64{{{1, 2}, {}}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Cube, want) {
		t.Errorf("NestColumns(nested)[0].Cube = %#v, want %#v", row.Cube, want)
	}
	if want := [][]int64{{3}, {4, 5}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Lhs, want) {
		t.Errorf("NestColumns(nested)[0].Lhs = %#v, want %#v", row.Lhs, want)
	}
	if want := [][]string{{"a"}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Rhs, want) {
		t.Errorf("NestColumns(nested)[0].Rhs = %#v, want %#v", row.Rhs, want)
	}
	if row.Deep == nil {
		t.Fatalf("NestColumns(nested)[0].Deep = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := [][][]string{{{"x"}}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*row.Deep, want) {
		t.Errorf("NestColumns(nested)[0].Deep = %#v, want %#v", *row.Deep, want)
	}

	null, err := queriesOver(keys, []any{
		[]any{}, []any{}, []any{}, nil,
	}).NestColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("NestColumns(deep: null) = error %v", err)
	}
	if null[0].Deep != nil {
		t.Errorf("NestColumns(deep: null)[0].Deep = %#v, want nil", null[0].Deep)
	}

	if _, err := queriesOver(keys, []any{
		[]any{[]any{int64(1)}}, []any{}, []any{}, nil,
	}).NestColumns(t.Context()); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("NestColumns(cube: [[int]]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
}

// A column whose declared width is ANY VALUE is read rather than
// asserted, the same claim TestAnythingReadsWhatTheGraphHolds makes of
// the property one emission over. `any` is a member of neither
// neo4j.PropertyValue nor neo4j.RecordValue, so the column has no
// constrained driver entry point to go through at all — and the null it
// exists to carry is the one value such an entry point could not have
// been written to carry.
func TestAnythingColumnsReadWhatTheGraphHolds(t *testing.T) {
	for _, want := range []any{
		nil, int64(1), 1.5, "x", true,
		[]any{int64(1), nil, "x"},
		map[string]any{"k": "v"},
	} {
		got, err := queriesOver([]string{"payload", "maybe"}, []any{want, want}).AnythingColumns(t.Context())
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("AnythingColumns(payload: %#v) = error %v", want, err)
			continue
		}
		if len(got) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("AnythingColumns(payload: %#v) returned %d rows, want 1", want, len(got))
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got[0].Payload, want) {
			t.Errorf("AnythingColumns(payload: %#v)[0].Payload = %#v", want, got[0].Payload)
		}
	}
}

// The nullable one carries the graph's null in its pointer. A record
// holds a key for every column the query projected, so a pointer spent
// on the missing key the Props map can have would be a pointer that is
// never nil — a null the caller has no way to read. This is the one
// place the column path and the entity path answer differently, and
// TestAnythingSeparatesAbsentFromNull is the other half of the pair.
func TestAnythingColumnsCarryTheirNull(t *testing.T) {
	null, err := queriesOver([]string{"payload", "maybe"}, []any{int64(1), nil}).AnythingColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AnythingColumns(maybe: null) = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(null) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("AnythingColumns(maybe: null) returned %d rows, want 1", len(null))
	}
	if null[0].Maybe != nil {
		t.Errorf("AnythingColumns(maybe: null)[0].Maybe = %#v, want nil", null[0].Maybe)
	}

	held, err := queriesOver([]string{"payload", "maybe"}, []any{int64(1), "v"}).AnythingColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AnythingColumns(maybe: \"v\") = error %v", err)
	}
	if held[0].Maybe == nil {
		t.Fatalf("AnythingColumns(maybe: \"v\")[0].Maybe = nil, want a pointer")
	}
	if *held[0].Maybe != any("v") {
		t.Errorf("AnythingColumns(maybe: \"v\")[0].Maybe points at %#v, want \"v\"", *held[0].Maybe)
	}

	// A column the record does not hold at all is neither of those: the
	// resolver committed it, so its absence is the driver disagreeing
	// with the plan rather than a value the graph held.
	if _, err := queriesOver([]string{"payload"}, []any{int64(1)}).AnythingColumns(t.Context()); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("AnythingColumns(no maybe) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
}
